en: The time or hour at which one retires to bed in order to sleep.

bedtime.ety: From Middle English bedtyme, bed-tyme, bedetyme, bedde tyme, equivalent to bed + time. Compare earlier Old English bedtīd (“bedtime”). Compare also West Frisian bêdtiid (“bedtime”), Dutch bedtijd (“bedtime”), Saterland Frisian Bädegungenstied (“bedtime”, literally “bed-goings-time”), German Low German Beddgahnstied, Bettgahnstiet (“bedtime”, literally “bed-goings-time”).

ex.ja: 父は寝るとき、よく本を読んでくれた。

ex.ja: 父は寝るとき、よく本を読んでくれた。

ex.en: My father used to read books to me at bedtime.
ex.ja: 父は寝るとき、よく本を読んでくれた。

note.ja: bed + time。「就寝時間」。

A glow; a flush of colour, especially pink or red.
To become red or pink in the face (and sometimes experience an associated feeling of warmth), especially due to shyness, love, shame, exc…
To be shy, ashamed, or embarrassed (to do something).

blush.ety:
From Middle English blusshen, bluschen, blusschen, blisshen, from Old English blysċan (“to be red; shine”), perhaps from Proto-Germanic *blaskijaną, from *blasǭ (“burning candle; torch”) or alternatively from Proto-Germanic *bluskijaną, from *blusjǭ (“torch”), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *bʰel-.
Cognate with Middle Low German blöschen (“to blush”). Compare also Old English blysian (“to burn; blaze”), Dutch blozen (“to blush”), Danish blusse (“to blush”), Old Norse blys (“torch”), Danish blus (“blaze”).

ex.en: When we made fun of her, she blushed.
ex.ja: 私たちがからかうと彼女は赤面した。

ex.en: I blush to think of such conduct.
ex.ja: そんなことをするなんて考えただけでも恥ずかしい。

ex.en: She turned away to hide her blushes.
ex.ja: 彼女は恥じらいの色を隠すために顔をそむけた。

note.ja: 古英語 blyscan（赤くなる）から。blaze（炎）と同系とされる。「顔を赤らめる・頬紅」。

A bread roll that is served with a savoury filling such as a hamburger or hot dog.
To form (the hair) into a bun.

The state or period of being imprisoned, confined, or enslaved.

captivity.ety: From Middle English captivite, from Latin captīvitās. By surface analysis, captive + -ity. Entered into the English lexicon around the 14th century.

ex.ja: 彼は捕虜になった。

note.ja: cap（つかむ）+ tiv + ity。つかまえられていること →「監禁・捕らわれの身」。captive（捕虜）。

A disaster beyond expectations.

en: Acting as a complement; making up a whole with something else.
Of the specific pairings of the bases in DNA and RNA.
A complementary colour.
An angle which adds with another to equal ninety degrees.

ex.ja: テレビと新聞は互いの機能を補完しあっている。

ex.en: It is likely that these two consonants are in complementary distribution.
ex.ja: この２つの子音は相補分布をなしていそうである。

note.ja: complement（補うもの）+ -ary。「補完的な」。complimentary（無料の）とつづりが似ているので注意。

en: An injury to part of the body, most especially the brain, caused by a violent blow, followed by loss of function.

concussion.ety: From Latin concussiō. Equivalent to concuss + -ion.

ex.ja: 脳震盪だとお医者さんに言われました。

ex.en: I had a concussion.
ex.ja: 脳しんとうを起こしました。

en: Rule by consuls, as during most periods of the Roman Republic or in France between 1799 and 1804.
The office of a consul, in its various senses.

consulate.ety: From Middle English consulat, consulate, from Latin consulātus, from consul + -ātus. In some senses, via French consulat. By surface analysis, consul + -ate (forms nouns denoting rank or office).

ex.en: He went out to the American consulate.
ex.ja: 彼はアメリカ領事館に出かけたよ。

ex.en: I work at the consulate.

ex.ja: 私はこのビザを、神戸のアメリカ領事館でとりました。

note.ja: consul（領事）+ -ate（官職・場所）。「領事館」。

en: To be in opposition; to contest; to dispute; to vie; to quarrel; to fight.
To struggle or exert oneself to obtain or retain possession of, or to defend.

contend.ety: From Middle English contenden, borrowed from Old French contendre, from Latin contendere (“to stretch out, extend, strive after, contend”), from com- (“together”) + tendere (“to stretch”); see tend, and compare attend, extend, intend, subtend.

ex.en: They contended with each other for the prize.
ex.ja: 彼らは賞を取ろうとお互いに競った。

ex.en: Several teams are contending for the prize.
ex.ja: いくつかのチームがその賞を勝ち取ろうと競い合っています。

ex.en: He had to contend against physical suffering.
ex.ja: 彼は肉体の苦痛と闘わねばならなかった。

note.ja: con（共に）+ tend（伸ばす・張る）。互いに張り合う →「争う・強く主張する」。

en: A strong desire; yearning.

craving.ety: From Middle English cravinge, from Old English crafing (“claim, demand”); equivalent to crave + -ing.

ex.en: I have a craving for fresh fruit.
ex.ja: 新鮮な果物が食べたいんだ。

ex.en: I've been craving frozen yogurt.
ex.ja: フローズン・ヨーグルトが食べたくてしょうがないんだよ。

ex.en: I suddenly got a craving to eat some crisp roast chicken skin.
ex.ja: 急激にかりかりした鳥皮が食べたくなった。

note.ja: crave（切望する）+ -ing。古英語 crafian（要求する）。「強い欲求」。

en: Relating to the practice of cookery or the activity of cooking.
Of or relating to a kitchen.

culinary.ety: Borrowed from French culinaire, itself a borrowing from Latin culīnārius, from culīna (“kitchen”).

note.ja: ラテン語 culina（台所）から。「料理の」。kiln（窯）と同系。

en: A loud noise; a cacophony or loud commotion.
To make a din, to resound.
(of a place) To be filled with sound, to resound.

din.ety:
From Middle English dyne, dynne, from Old English dyne, from Proto-West Germanic *duni, from Proto-Germanic *duniz, from Proto-Indo-European *dʰún-is, from *dʰwen- (“to make a noise”).
Cognate with English tone, Sanskrit धुनि (dhúni, “sounding”), ध्वनति (dhvánati, “to make a noise, to roar”), Old Norse dynr, Norwegian Nynorsk dynja, Swedish dån, dön.

ex.en: His voice was heard above the din.
ex.ja: 彼の声が騒音にも負けずに聞こえた。

note.ja: 古英語 dyne（騒音）から。「騒音」。

en: Separate; distinct; individual; non-continuous.
That can be perceived individually, not as connected to, or part of, something else.

discrete.ety: From Old French discret, from Latin discrētus, past participle of discernō (“divide”), from dis- + cernō (“sift”). Doublet of discreet.

en: To disagree; to withhold assent. Construed with from (or, formerly, to).
To differ from, especially in opinion, beliefs, etc.
Disagreement with the ideas, doctrines, decrees, etc. of a political party, government or religion.
An act of disagreeing with, or deviating from, the views and opinions of those holding authority.

dissent.ety: From Middle English dissenten, from Latin dissentiō, dissentīre (“to differ in sentiments, disagree, be at odds, contradict, quarrel”), from dis- + sentiō, sentīre (see sense).

ex.en: He dissented from the opinion of the majority.
ex.ja: 彼は大多数の意見に異議を唱えた。

ex.en: I dissent from what he said.
ex.ja: 私は彼の言ったことに反対する。

ex.en: Within the rape crisis movement, Greensite's dissent is significant.
ex.ja: レイプ危機運動の内部においては、グリーンサイトによる異議表明は重要な意義を持っている。

note.ja: dis（離れて）+ sent（感じる）。違うように感じる →「異議（を唱える）」。consent（同意）と対。

en: Noteworthy, remarkable, great.
Distinguished, important, noteworthy.

eminent.ety: From Middle French éminent, from Latin present participle ēminēns, ēminentis, from verb ēmineō (“to project, protrude”), from ex- (“out of, from”) + mineō, related to mons (English mount). ex.ja: 彼は教師としても作家としても著名である。

ex.ja: 彼はいくつもの大発見で有名だ。

ex.en: Mr Smith is an eminent violinist.
ex.ja: スミス氏は著名なバイオリニストである。

To attempt through application of effort (to do something); to try strenuously.
To work with purpose.

endeavor.ety: The verb is from Middle English endeveren (“to make an effort”); the noun is from Middle English endevour, from the verb. ex.en: He made an endeavor to improve the situation.
ex.ja: 彼は事態を改善しようと努力した。

ex.en: She endeavored to live up to their expectations.
ex.ja: 彼女は彼らの期待にそうよう努力した。

ex.en: I'm sure your endeavor will bear fruit.
ex.ja: きっと努力が実を結びますよ。

note.ja: en + devoir（義務）。「義務を果たそうとする」→「努力」。duty と同系。

en: A person filled with or guided by enthusiasm.

enthusiast.ety: From Ancient Greek ἐνθουσιαστής (enthousiastḗs, “an enthusiast, a zealot”), from ἐνθουσιάζειν (enthousiázein, “(intransitive) be inspired or possessed by a god, be rapt, be in ecstasy, (transitive) inspire”): see enthusiasm.

ex.en: He is much more of a golf enthusiast than I am.

A female of other bird species, particularly a sexually mature female fowl.

ex.en: This is the perfect place for an ambush.
ex.ja: ここは待ち伏せするには、もってこいの場所だよ。

ex.en: He has a plan to ambush him.
ex.ja: 彼を待ち伏せる一計を案じた。

ex.en: It's the perfect place for an ambush.
ex.ja: ここは待ち伏せするには、もってこいの場所だよ。

note.ja: 古フランス語 embuschier（茂みに隠れる）から。en + busche（茂み）。bush と同じ。「待ち伏せ」。

en: To make better; improve.
To become better.
An act of righting a wrong; compensation.

amend.ety: From Middle English amenden, from Old French amender, from Latin ēmendō (“free from faults”), from ex (“from, out of”) + mendum (“fault”). Compare aphetic mend. Doublet of emend.

ex.en: It's never too late to make amends.
ex.ja: 過ちを改むるにはばかることなかれ。

ex.en: Some people want to amend the constitution.
ex.ja: 憲法を改正したいと考えている人たちがいる。

ex.en: He will make amends for the damage.
ex.ja: 彼は損害の償いをするだろう。

note.ja: ラテン語 emendare（欠点を取り除く）から。e（外へ）+ menda（欠点）。「改正する」。mend（直す）も同じ。

en: The state of being arrogant; a type of extreme or foolish pride in which someone feels much superior to another.

arrogance.ety: From Middle English arrogaunce, from Middle French arrogance, from Latin arrogantia.

ex.en: I cannot stand his arrogance any longer.
ex.ja: 私は彼の傲慢さにこれ以上我慢できない。

ex.en: I can't stand his arrogance any longer.
ex.ja: 私は彼の傲慢さにもうこれ以上我慢できない。

ex.en: I cannot put up with his arrogance.
ex.ja: 私は彼の傲慢な態度が我慢できない。

note.ja: arrogant（傲慢な）+ -ance。ad + rogare（求める）。「（権利を）要求すること」→「傲慢さ」。

en: A person who is in attendance or in the audience of an event.
A person who is attended.

ex.en: The meeting had 12 attendees.
ex.ja: この会議は１２人で構成されている。

note.ja: attend（出席する）+ -ee（〜する人）。「出席者」。

en: Of, from or relating to Australia; Australian.

Aussie.ety:
From a clipping of Australian (or Australia) + -ie.
The spelling likely adopted the visual template of the pre‐existing personal diminutive Aussie (from Austin or Augusta). However, while the personal nickname retains standard English phonics with a voiceless /s/, the pronunciation of the national slang (/ˈɒzi/) was driven by a highly productive morphophonological template in Commonwealth slang that strongly favors short stressed vowels and lenited consonants.
The clipped base promotes the historically unstressed initial vowel to the short /ɒ/. This reflects a broader Commonwealth phonological

note.ja: Australian のくだけた短縮。「オーストラリア人」。

en: A Christian sacrament, by which one is received into a church and sometimes given a name, generally involving the candidate to be anointe…
A similar ceremony of initiation, purification or naming.

baptism.ety: From Middle English bapteme, baptesme, from Old French batesme or bapteme, from Ecclesiastical Latin, Late Latin baptisma, from Ancient Greek βάπτισμα (báptisma, “dipping, baptism”), from βαπτίζω (baptízō, “I dip in liquid”). Displaced native Old English fulwiht.

note.ja: ギリシャ語 baptizein（水に浸す）から。「洗礼」。

en: A fellow, a man; especially an ordinary man, a man on the street.
An exemplar of a certain masculine, independent male archetype.

bloke.ety:
Origin unknown; the following borrowings have been hypothesized:
* From a modern Celtic language, such as Irish bloc (“block”) or Scottish Gaelic ploc (“large, stubborn person”, literally “block of wood”), themselves borrowings from English block
* From Hindustani لوک (lok) / लोक (lok, “people, folk”) or Shelta loke (“man”).

ex.en: There aren't many blokes that nice!
ex.ja: あんないい男そうそういないぞ！！

ex.en: I don't want to talk to that bloke ever again.
ex.ja: あんな奴とはもう二度と口をききたくない。

note.ja: 語源ははっきりしない。（英）「男・やつ」。

en: Of a bleached or pale golden (light yellowish) colour.
Particularly of a person, having blond hair.
A pale yellowish (golden brown) color, especially said of hair color.
A person with this hair color.
To color or dye blond.

blond.ety:
Borrowed from Middle French blond m, from Old French blond, blont, blund, (> Medieval Latin blondus), from Frankish *blund (“a mixed color between golden and light-brown”), from Proto-Germanic *blundaz (“mixed, blinding”), from Proto-Indo-European *bʰlendʰ- (“to become turbid, see badly, go blind”). Compare Old English blondenfeax (“grey-haired”), Old English blandan (“to mix”). See more at blend.
An alternative etymology connects Frankish *blund to Proto-Germanic *blundaz (“blond”), from Proto-Indo-European *bʰl̥ndʰ-, *bʰlendʰ- (“blond, red-haired”). If so, then it would be cognate with Sansk

ex.en: His hair is blond and he looks young.
ex.ja: 彼の髪は金髪で、彼は若く見える。

ex.en: The boy has a shock of blond hair.
ex.ja: その少年の髪は金髪でもじゃもじゃだ。

ex.en: He has blue eyes and blond hair.
ex.ja: 彼は青い目と金髪である。

note.ja: フランス語 blond（金髪の）から。女性には blonde の綴りも使う。

en: To make indistinct or hazy, to obscure or dim.
To smear, stain or smudge.
A smear, smudge or blot.
Something that appears hazy or indistinct.
Lacking awareness; clueless or confused.

blur.ety: From earlier blurre, probably an alteration of blear, from Middle English bleren, from Old English *blerian (attested in āblered (“made bare, made bald”)), from Proto-West Germanic *blaʀjan, from Proto-Germanic *blazjaną (“to make pale”), from Proto-Germanic *blasaz (“pale”). Compare Scots blore, bloar (“to blur, cover with blots”), Low German bleeroged (“blear-eyed”). More at blear.

ex.en: The TV picture was blurred.
ex.ja: テレビの画像はぼやけて見えた。

ex.en: Close things look blurred.
ex.ja: 近くの物がかすんで見えます。

ex.en: The mountain was blurred by fog.
ex.ja: 霧のため山の輪郭がぼんやりしていた。

note.ja: 語源ははっきりしない。blear（かすむ）と同系とされる。「ぼやける」。

en: A part or division of the intestines, usually the large intestine.
The entrails or intestines; the internal organs of the stomach.

bowel.ety: Borrowed from Middle French bouel, from Old French boïel, from Latin botellus, diminutive of botulus (“sausage”). Doublet of boyau.

ex.en: I have not had a bowel movement for a week.
ex.ja: １週間便通がない。

ex.en: I have trouble with my bowels.
ex.ja: 腸の具合が悪い。

ex.en: It moves the bowels.
ex.ja: お通じがよくなりますよ。

note.ja: ラテン語 botellus（小さなソーセージ）から。「腸」。

en: The bony ridge over the eyes, upon which the eyebrows are located.
The eyebrow.
To bound or limit; to be at, or form, the edge of.

brow.ety:
From Middle English browe, from Old English brū, from Proto-West Germanic *brāwu, from Proto-Germanic *brūwō, from Proto-Indo-European *h₃bʰrúHs (“brow”).
Cognate with Scots broo (“brow”), Dutch brauw (“brow”), German Braue (“eyebrow”), Danish, Norwegian Nynorsk and Swedish bryn (“brow”), Faroese, Icelandic brún (“brow”). See also Middle Irish brúad, Tocharian B pärwāne (“eyebrows”), Lithuanian bruvi̇̀s, Serbo-Croatian obrva (“eyebrow”), Russian бровь (brovʹ, “brow”), Ancient Greek ὀφρύς (ophrús, “eyebrow”), Sanskrit भ्रू (bhrū, “eyebrow”)), Persian ابرو (abru, “eyebrow”), Khowar بروُ (bruú, “

ex.en: The old woman knitted her brows.
ex.ja: その老婦人はまゆをひそめた。

ex.en: I felt the sweat trickle down my brow.
ex.ja: 汗が額を滴り落ちるのを感じた。

ex.en: Tom wrinkled his brow like he was displeased.
ex.ja: トムは不機嫌そうに額に皺を寄せた。

note.ja: 古英語 brū（眉）から。「眉・額」。eyebrow。

en: An edible plant (Brassica oleracea var. capitata) having a head of green leaves.
Any of various cultivars of the species Brassica oleracea.
To form a head like that of the cabbage.

Some authorities derive it from Latin caput (“head”), others from ca- (said to be an expressive prefix) + boce (“hump; bump”) (whence English boss).

ex.en: Can I have seconds on rice and cabbage?
ex.ja: ライスとキャベツをお代わりお願いします。

ex.en: We talked about cabbages and kings.
ex.ja: 私たちはいろんなことを話しました。

ex.en: The price of cabbage fell because of overproduction.
ex.ja: キャベツは生産過剰で値をくずした。

note.ja: 古北フランス語 caboche（頭）から。頭の形の野菜 →「キャベツ」。capital と同系。

en: A division of a political unit.
One of the states comprising the Swiss Confederation.
To delineate as a separate district.
To divide into cantons.

canton.ety: 1530s, from Middle French canton, from Old French canton (“corner”); heraldic sense from the 1570s, geographic sense from c. 1600.

ex.en: I live in Canton.
ex.ja: 広州に住んでいる。

note.ja: 古フランス語 canton（隅・地区）から。「（スイスの）州」。

en: To provide, particularly
To provide with food, especially for a special occasion as a professional service.
A method of ringing nine bells in four pairs with a ninth tenor bell.

cater.ety: From Middle English catour (“acater, provisioner”), aphetic form of acatour (“acater”), from Old French acater (“to buy, to purchase”). Equivalent to cate + -er.

ex.en: This is a store that caters specially to students.
ex.ja: これは学生相手の店です。

ex.en: Our travel advice center caters to the independent traveler.
ex.ja: 我が旅行相談センターは個人旅行者にサービスを提供する。

ex.en: Tom has tastes in food that are difficult to cater for.
ex.ja: トムは味にうるさい。

note.ja: 古フランス語 acater（買う）から。「食料を調達する」→「仕出しする・（要求に）応える」。catering と同じ。

en: A vertical tube or hollow column used to emit environmentally polluting gaseous and solid matter (including but not limited to by-product…
The glass flue surrounding the flame of an oil lamp.
To negotiate a chimney (narrow vertical cave passage) by pushing against the sides with back, feet, hands, etc.

chimney.ety: From Middle English chymeneye, chymneye, chymene, from Old French cheminee, from Late Latin camīnāta, from Latin camīnus, from Ancient Greek κάμῑνος (kámīnos, “furnace”). Doublet of chimenea.

ex.en: The chimney began to give out smoke.
ex.ja: 煙突は煙を出し始めた。

ex.en: Black smoke came out of the chimney.
ex.ja: 煙突から黒い煙が出てきた。

ex.en: This chimney has begun to draw badly.
ex.ja: この煙突は通りが悪くなった。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 kaminos（炉）からラテン語・フランス語を経た語。「煙突」。

en: Covered with or characterised by clouds.
Not transparent or clear.

cloudy.ety: From Middle English cloudy (“cloudy, overcast, gloomy, dark", also "hilly, rocky”), from Old English clūdiġ (“stony, rocky”), equivalent to cloud + -y.

ex.en: It's getting cloudy. It may rain soon.
ex.ja: くもってきた。やがて雨になるかもしれない。

ex.en: It was cloudy all day long today.
ex.ja: 今日は一日中くもっていた。

ex.en: All of a sudden, it became cloudy.
ex.ja: 突然、空が曇ってきた。

note.ja: cloud（雲）+ -y。「曇った・濁った」。

ja: 色彩豊かな（英国のつづり）

en: British standard spelling of colorful.

ex.en: I saw a boy with colourful shoes.
ex.ja: カラフルな靴を履いた男の子を見たんだ。

ex.en: Women like colourful umbrellas.
ex.ja: 女性はカラフルな傘を好む。

note.ja: colorful のイギリスのつづり。「色彩豊かな」。

en: Having, feeling or showing compassion (to or toward someone).
Given to someone as an exception because of a family emergency or a death in their family.

compassionate.ety: Pseudo-Latinism, derived from a pseudo-Latin form of French compassionné, past participle of compassionner (“to feel sorry for”). By surface analysis, compassion + -ate.

note.ja: compassion（思いやり）+ -ate。com（共に）+ pati（苦しむ）。「共に苦しむ」→「思いやりのある」。patient と同じ。

en: Able to be exchanged, one for the other, especially
Able to be exchanged for specie.
A convertible car: a car with a removable or foldable roof able to convert from a closed to open vehicle and back again.
A convertible security: a stock, bond, etc. that can be turned into another (usually common stock) under certain set terms.

convertible.ety: From Old French convertible, from Late Latin convertibilis (“interchangeable”), from Latin convertere (“to turn back, to turn over, to turn around, to turn upside down”), from con- (“with, together”) + vertere (“to turn”), + -ibilis (“-ible: able to”). Equivalent to convert + -ible.

ex.en: I'd like to drive across the USA in a convertible.
ex.ja: コンバーチブルでアメリカを横断したい。

ex.en: I'd like to drive across the USA in a convertible car.
ex.ja: コンバーチブルでアメリカを横断したい。

ex.en: My new Alfa Romeo convertible is light red.
ex.ja: 私の新しいアルファ・ロメオのオープンカーは明るい赤色だ。

note.ja: con（すっかり）+ vert（向ける）+ ible。向きを変えられる →「転換できる・オープンカー（屋根を変えられる車）」。

en: A hemispherical pit created by the impact of a meteorite or other object.
The basin-like opening or mouth of a volcano, through which the chief eruption comes; similarly, the mouth of a geyser, about which a con…
To form craters in a surface.
To collapse catastrophically; to become devastated or completely destroyed.

crater.ety: First coined 1613, from Latin crātēr (“basin”), from Ancient Greek κρᾱτήρ (krātḗr, “mixing-bowl, wassail-bowl”).

ex.en: There are many craters on the moon.
ex.ja: 月にはたくさんのクレーターがある。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 kratēr（酒を混ぜる鉢）から。鉢の形 →「噴火口・クレーター」。

en: Incorporating all current and previous data up to the present or at the time of measuring or collating.
That is formed by an accumulation of successive additions.

en: A person who manages, administers or organizes a collection, either independently or employed by a museum, library, archive or zoo.
One appointed to act as guardian of the estate of a person not legally competent to manage it, or of an absentee; a trustee.

curator.ety: From Latin cūrātor (“one who has care of a thing, a manager, guardian, trustee”), from cūrāre (“to take care of”), from cūra (“care, heed, attention, anxiety, grief”).

note.ja: ラテン語 curare（世話をする）+ -tor。「世話をする人」→「学芸員・キュレーター」。cure、curious と同じ cur。

en: Synonym of divinity: the state, position, or fact of being a god.
A supernatural divine being; a god or goddess.

deity.ety: From Middle French deité, from Latin deitās.

ex.en: Do you know which deity this temple is dedicated to?
ex.ja: この寺の本尊は何であるか知っていますか。

note.ja: ラテン語 deitas（神性）から。deus（神）。「神」。divine と同系。

en: The act of despairing or becoming desperate; a giving up of hope.
A state of despair, or utter hopelessness; abandonment of hope.

desperation.ety: From Middle English desperacion, desperacioun, desperation, disparacion, disperacion, disperacioun, dispiracioune, dysperacioun, from Middle French desperation and its etymon Latin dēspērātiō, dēspērātiōnis. By surface analysis, desperate + -ion.

ex.en: We arrived at that plan out of pure desperation, but the book sold well.
ex.ja: 苦肉の策で企画したんですが、その本はよく売れました。

ex.en: To tell the truth, she gave away all her money to others in desperation.
ex.ja: 実のところ、彼女はやけになって、有り金をみんな人にやってしまったのだ。

ex.en: In a few seconds I would have overcome the desperation threshold.
ex.ja: 後数秒で私は絶望の分岐点を越えるのだ。

note.ja: desperate（必死の）+ -ion。de（離れて）+ sperare（希望する）。「絶望・必死」。

en: Causing damage or harm.
Anything harmful.

detrimental.ety: From Medieval Latin *dētrīmentālis, from Latin dētrīmentum (“harm”), from dēterō (“to rub off, wear”), from dē- (“down, away”) + terō (“to rub or grab”).

ex.en: Building up too much stress has a detrimental effect on your health.
ex.ja: ストレスを溜めすぎると健康に悪影響を及ぼす。

note.ja: ラテン語 detrimentum（すり減らすこと）から。de（下に）+ tri（こする）+ ment。→「有害な」。

en: A gastrointestinal disorder characterized by frequent and very soft or watery bowel movements.
The watery or very soft excrement that comes from such bowel movements.

diarrhea.ety:
From Middle English diaria, from Middle French diarrie (French diarrhée), from Late Latin diarrhoea, from Ancient Greek διάρροια (diárrhoia, “through-flowing”), from διά (diá, “through”) + ῥέω (rhéō, “flow”). By surface analysis, dia- + -rrhea. Spelling later altered to resemble the word's Latin and Greek roots.
Displaced native Old English ūtsiht (literally “straining out”).

ex.en: I have a touch of diarrhea.
ex.ja: 下痢気味です。

ex.en: Here's some medicine for diarrhea.
ex.ja: 下痢止めです。

ex.en: I've had diarrhea since yesterday.
ex.ja: 昨日から下痢が続いているんです。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 diarrhoia（流れ出ること）から。dia（通して）+ rhein（流れる）。「下痢」。rhythm と同じ rhein。

en: inclined, minded
Having a certain disposition.

ex.en: The committee was not disposed to hold another meeting.
ex.ja: 委員会はもう一度会議を開きたくなかった。

ex.en: The high salary disposed him to accept the position.
ex.ja: 高給なので彼はその地位を引き受ける気になった。

ex.en: The judge disposed of the case in short order.
ex.ja: 裁判官は非常にすばやくその訴訟を片づけた。

note.ja: dispose（配置する）+ -ed。「（心が）向けられた」→「〜したい気がする」。

en: An act of distorting.
A result of distorting.

distortion.ety: Borrowed from Latin distortio, distortionis, from distortus.

note.ja: dis（離れて）+ tort（ねじる）+ ion。ねじ曲げること →「ゆがみ・歪曲」。

en: Relating to a doctorate.
Pertaining to a medical doctor or physician.

doctoral.ety: From doctor + -al, probably modelled on Latin doctorālis.

note.ja: doctor（博士）+ -al。「博士の」。

A person's perceived but unjustified right to something; a tendency to claim what one does not deserve.

ex.ja: 私は自分を映画のやくざと同一視した。

note.ja: academy + -ia。プラトンが教えた森アカデメイア（Akadēmeia）から。「学界」。

en: The act of altering or making different.
A minor adjustment to clothing, such as hemming or shortening, to make it fit better.

alteration.ety: From Old French alteracion (French altération), from Medieval Latin alterātiō. Morphologically alter + -ation.

ex.en: How long will it take for alterations?
ex.ja: 直しはどれくらいかかりますか。

ex.en: The sales plan allows of no alteration.
ex.ja: 販売計画は変更の余地が無い。

ex.en: The plan is incapable of alteration.
ex.ja: その計画は変更の余地がない。

note.ja: alter（変える）+ -ation。ラテン語 alter（もう一方の）。「別のものにすること」→「変更」。alternative と同じ。

en: To make clear or effective.
To speak clearly; to enunciate.
Clear; effective.
Speaking in a clear and effective manner; having both good articulation and good elocution.
An animal of the subkingdom Articulata.

articulate.ety: The adjective is first attested in 1531, the verb in 1551; borrowed from Latin articulātus (“distinct, articulated, jointed”), perfect passive participle of articulō, see -ate (etymology 1, 2 and 3). Regular participial usage of the adjective up until Early Modern English.

ex.en: Our baby is not yet articulate.
ex.ja: うちの赤ん坊はまだちゃんとしゃべれない。

ex.en: He works fast and is very articulate but his insincerity is his biggest defect.
ex.ja: 手八丁口八丁の彼だけど、誠がないのが玉に瑕だね。

note.ja: ラテン語 articulare（関節に分ける）から。articulus（小さな関節）。「区切ってはっきり話す」。article と同じ。
